To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the resonant properties of $^{18}$ Ne have been investigated by means of resonant elastic scattering.

(1) the $J$=1$^{\pm}$ resonances at 6.28 MeV and 6.35 MeV were observed for the first time in the $^{17}$O+$p$ reaction, and the $^{14}$$\mathrm{O}(\alpha,p)^{17}$F reaction rate was determined for the first time.
we have observed five resonances in $^{17}$O+$p$ resonant scattering and assigned $J^{\Pi}$=1$^{-}$ to the 6 MeV resonance that dominates the thermonouclear rate below 1 Gk.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the resonant states in $^{18}Ne$ and the thermonuclear rate $^{14}O(\alpha,p)^{17}F$, which is one of the important reaction rates in the breakout from CNO cycle to $rp$ process in type I xray bursts.
the $^{14}O(\alpha,p)^{17}F$ reaction, which is a crucial reaction for the breakout from the CNO cycles to the rp-process during type I x-ray bursters.
the study of the $^{18}$F($p$,$\gamma$)$^{19}$Ne reaction, which is one of the most important reactions in the rp-process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the $^{14}O(\alpha,p)^{17}F$ breakout reaction rate has been significantly reduced at low temperatures.
our new rate is significantly lower than the previously recommended rate by Caughlan and Fowler (CaF) and higher than that by the JINA reaclib database.

the new $^{18}$F(p, $\alpha$)$^{15}$O rate is consistent with previous results, and that the new $R$-process rates of the $^{18}$N($\alpha$,p) and $^{18}$C(p, $\alpha)$ reactions are consistent with previous results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the $^{14}O(\alpha,p)^{17}$F breakout reaction rate is significantly reduced by the new resonance data, and thus the rp-process path to $^{20}$F is less likely to be blocked in the hot-CNO burning.
the present study provides a reliable thermonuclear rate for the $^{14}O(\alpha,p)^{17}F$ reaction, which is important for the breakout from the CNO cycle to the $rp$ process in x-ray bursts.

the thermonuclear rate has been determined with a precision of a factor of 2, and the $J$=1$^-, 2^-, 3^-$ and 4$^-$ resonances at $^{18}$F($\alpha$)$^{22}$Ne are the most important for the breakout reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermonuclear rate is significantly higher than previous estimates, and the breakout from the CNO cycle is much more efficient in the hot CNO cycle.
the $^{14}O$($\alpha$, $p$)$^{1}$7$F$ reaction rate at temperatures below 1 GK is significantly reduced by a factor of about 3-5 compared to that obtained in the previous work.

the $^{14}O(\alpha,p)^{17}F$ reaction has been well determined for the temperature range 0.1 GK$\leq$T$\leq$1.5 GK, and the $^{14,15}O(\alpha,n)^{17,18}F$ reactions are now well constrained for T$\leq$0.5 GK.
